saints.name: St. Fulbert of Chartres
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop and teacher who made Chartres a beacon of learning and rebuilt its great cathedral…
biography: Fulbert was born about 960 and studied under Gerbert of Aurillac, the future Pope Sylvester II. As master of the cathedral school of Chartres he made it one of the foremost centres of learning in Europe, drawing students from many lands and earning the affectionate title of “venerable Socrates” from his pupils.

Chosen Bishop of Chartres in 1006, he was a wise and charitable pastor, a counsellor to kings, and a firm opponent of abuses. When his cathedral burned in 1020 he began the great rebuilding whose crypt survives to this day. Devoted to the Blessed Virgin, he composed sermons and hymns in her honour, especially for the feast of her Nativity, and died in 1028.
saints.knownFor: The school of Chartres and the rebuilding of its cathedral.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 10 April
